name: Lifted F-450 dually
_note_licensing: PLACEHOLDER PLATE. This photo predates the visualizer and its rights are unconfirmed — it must not stay on a public page. Replace with a photo DROOOLY owns or has licensed before this ships as the default view. Everything below is calibration, not authorship; swapping the image is a new JSON plus one calibration pass.
_note_angle: This is a front-three-quarter shot, not a true side profile. The FRONT wheel is near-circular (aspect 1.01) so a head-on render composites onto it convincingly. The REAR is a 3:1 ellipse — far too oblique to swap — so it is marked usable:false rather than rendered wrong. A true side profile makes both wheels usable.
_note_scale: referenceWheelDiaIn is an ESTIMATE read off the photo, not a spec. Absolute sizing therefore carries that error, but every RELATIVE change (22 vs 26 vs 30) is exact, because it is a ratio against this number. A plate we shoot ourselves gets a known wheel and this becomes measured.

wheels.reason: Too oblique in this shot — the wheel reads as a 3:1 ellipse and a head-on render cannot be made to sit in it honestly.

_note_layers: A flat photo can only have a wheel pasted onto it. Making the tire, offset, front width and lift do anything needs the plate cut into layers: background with the wheels removed and the wells filled, the body separable so lift can move it, and a foreground of fender lips that must overlap the tire. That is per-angle handwork, which is why a small set of well-prepared angles beats a full 360 on day one.
